title: Centralize VPC egress authorization + private DNS Terraform module
creator: Aisha Thompson
description:
Goal: Build a reusable Terraform module (tf-privnet-egress-guard) to centralize and enforce VPC egress authorization, default deny outbound posture, and private DNS routing for Redwood Private deployments. The module must be cloud-agnostic by providing provider-specific submodules (AWS/GCP abstraction), support both centralized egress (NAT/egress-proxy) and distributed egress patterns, and integrate with our existing Private control plane configs.

Scope:
- Security Groups and Network ACL scaffolding with defend-by-default rules, configurable allowlists based on tags and CIDR blocks.
- Optional managed NAT / egress-proxy attachment with health-check-backed failover.
- Private DNS: automated creation of private hosted zones, Route53/Cloud DNS resolver rules (split-horizon), and resolver forwarding to on-prem or partner DNS.
- Egress policies: declarative allowlists, service endpoints, and URL-based egress gating (via proxy integration).
- Health checks and observability hooks: Terraform outputs for health-check endpoints, integration points for Console (rollup metrics), and automated smoke tests.
- Upgrade path: clear versioning, migration guides for state changes, import helpers, and CI-driven automated upgrades with canary flag in Dedicated clusters.

Acceptance criteria (must pass before merge):
1) Module implements deny-all outbound by default and exposes a minimal allowlist interface (tags, security_group_refs, cidr_blocks).
2) Private DNS automation creates/updates private hosted zones and resolver rules without manual steps; supports safe rollback.
3) Egress path supports central NAT and egress-proxy options; module exposes variables to switch patterns per environment.
4) Health checks: deployed NAT/proxy targets register health endpoints; Terraform exposes outputs and SSM parameter names for orchestration tests.
5) CI runs terratest/integration tests across small infra sandbox and validates connectivity, DNS resolution, and policy enforcement.
6) Documentation: PRD + module README, upgrade notes, and sample usage in dedicated/private configs.

Design notes and constraints:
- Prefer composition: top-level module delegates to aws/ gcp submodules. Keep core API stable (inputs/outputs).
- Avoid provider-specific hardcoding in end-user configs; provide examples per cloud.
- NACL changes are disruptive; module will default to signaling a 'manual review required' if NACL delta is non-empty unless override flag set.
- Private DNS resolver rules require cross-account permissions in some org setups; document permission checklist and provide helper IAM policy snippets.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (sandbox): land module with aws-only path, run terratest, and validate for 2 internal sandboxes. (owner: Diego)
- Phase 2 (pilot): roll into one Dedicated customer staging environment behind feature-flag; gather metrics and upgrade notes.
- Phase 3 (general availability): publish to registry, update reference stacks, and coordinate with Solutions Eng for customer migrations.
